Subject: Post-call: FintechAI pricing & latency trade-offs

Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Usage profile (your notes): 30M tokens/month baseline, with spiky peaks during batch runs and product demos.
- Primary flows: interactive user queries (p95 target <=250ms), background enrichment jobs (can tolerate higher latency).
- Budget: you mentioned an internal range ~ $10k–$15k/mo for inference initially. You also asked for a target $/1M tokens baseline for unit economics.
- Key trade-offs we discussed: Dedicated vs Hosted tiers, batching windows for throughput, streaming to optimize perceived latency, and quantization options to lower costs.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Confirm the 30M/month estimate and expected growth cadence (Q-over-Q).
2) Share a sample traffic split (interactive vs batch %).
3) Any hard SLOs for p50/p95/p99 or SLA requirements.

Proposed next step: I'll put together a quick estimate that compares Hosted vs Dedicated unit costs ($/1M tokens) and show the impact of quantization and batching on unit economics. Vivek (cc'd) can join a short technical deep-dive to size batching windows and streaming config.

Attaching: redwood_cost_unit_econ_v1.xlsx (estimates) and a draft mutual action plan.

Thanks — talk soon.

On SLOs: for our consumer-facing query path we need p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 600ms. Background jobs can be >1s.

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround and the requirements doc. Attached is a concise breakdown (estimates_20260610.pdf) — high level numbers below so you can feed them into procurement: 

Summary (high-level, tailored to your 30M/mo profile):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): estimated $1,800 per 1M tokens. No committed capacity; good for fast start and lower operational overhead.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity, 12-month commit example): estimated $1,100 per 1M tokens at 30M/mo steady state. Includes reserved GPU pool, better unit cost and predictable throughput.
- Quantization: 8-bit (INT8) typically reduces token cost ~20–30%; 4-bit can add another ~10–15% but may need eval for quality impact. Exact savings depend on model family and accuracy tolerance.
- Batching vs Streaming: larger batching windows (50–200ms) can reduce unit cost by increasing throughput efficiency but increases tail latency. Streaming + small batching windows (10–30ms) is our recommendation for interactive traffic to keep perceived latency low while capturing some batching gains.

Trade-offs / recommendation for your use case:
- Pilot (30 days): start on Hosted or a short Dedicated eval with small commit to validate quality and baselines. Instrument p95/p99 and token volumes.
- Production: if volumes stay ~30M+/mo, move to Dedicated reserved capacity (saves ~30–40% on unit cost vs Hosted in our estimate).

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical deep-dive with Vivek to lock down batching windows, batch size targets, and streaming config (15–30m).
2) Finance: I'll send a focused pricing worksheet and a draft mutual action plan for signature.

Let me know times that work for the deep-dive next week.

Subject: Re: Post-call: FintechAI pricing & latency trade-offs — technical notes

Alex — quick tech notes ahead of the deep-dive: 

- Interactive path: use streaming RPCs + small batching (10–30ms window) and dynamic batch packing based on sequence length. This preserves perceived latency while squeezing in short batches. For p95 ~250ms goal, aim for a 20ms batching window in region with p95 network <50ms.
- Background/enrichment: larger windows (50–200ms) and larger batch sizes; enable KV cache reuse for prefix-heavy workloads to cut per-token compute.
- Quantization: start with 8-bit for production trials; run a 2–3 week eval comparing end-to-end quality (A/B on key prompts) before moving to 4-bit.
- Autoscale & fallbacks: configure two tiers — primary reserved pool + overflow to hosted variant with automatic fallback and degraded SLOs. This keeps availability during bursts without overcommitting.

Happy to walk through a sample config in the call. Propose Tue/Wed next week for a 30m slot.

—
